prize_parts.citation: For the conception and leadership of the ATLAS and CMS experiments, which led to the experimental discovery of the Higgs boson

statement.case_for: The 2012 observation of the Higgs boson is the clearest discovery on the shortlist: a concrete new particle, predicted decades earlier, found independently by two experiments and then characterised in detail through couplings, spin and parity. The 2013 prize honoured the theory only, so the experimental half of the story remains unrecognised and the gap grows with time. It is the one case where the discovery itself sits at the centre and the question is only who the people behind it are. The founding proposers and long-term leaders of ATLAS and CMS (Della Negra, Jenni, Virdee) are the people whose detector concepts made the discovery possible, and recognising the instrument-building leadership is more defensible than choosing spokespersons of a given year.
statement.case_against: Credit is spread over thousands of physicists in two collaborations, and any three-person selection is a compromise that omits real contributors. It is also genuinely arguable that Gianotti, as ATLAS spokesperson at the announcement, belongs in place of Della Negra. Attribution is the weakest point, and several colleagues rank other cases higher: circuit QED and optical lattice clocks have more compact, cleaner credit and much stronger opening support. I also rely on memory for the precise roles of the named individuals.

responses.point: Mehlig ranked circuit QED first, as a clear step beyond the macroscopic quantum tunnelling work recognised in 2025, while placing the Higgs experimental discovery second as the remaining half of the Standard Model story.
responses.response: I agree with his reading of the Higgs case and his naming of Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee as the conceivers and leaders of the detectors. On circuit QED I accept that it is a distinct architectural step, but it is closer to an enabling technology than to a discovery, and the adjacency to the 2025 prize still concerns me. I would not call it wrong, only my second or third choice.

responses.point: Pearce ranked IceCube first and proposed Gianotti, Jenni and Virdee for the Higgs, dropping Della Negra and acknowledging that choosing three from four is a hard call.
responses.response: I take seriously his argument that Gianotti led ATLAS at the discovery, but spokesperson terms are rotating and tied to the moment of announcement, whereas Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee conceived the detectors and carried them for decades. I would defend the founders. I disagree on IceCube as the lead: the diffuse flux is a real discovery, but the origin of most of the flux is unresolved and the source identifications are younger, so I place it behind the Higgs on maturity.

responses.point: Kroll ranked optical lattice clocks first, arguing that the Katori and Ye pairing is clean, mature and consistent with the principle that progress is limited by measurement.
responses.response: I grant that this has the cleanest attribution on the list, and I regard it as a serious alternative. My reservation is that it is an invention and precision tool whose decisive discovery payoff, such as a redefined second or a new test of fundamental constants, has not yet arrived, and the 2005 frequency-comb prize covers part of the lineage. I would rather recognise the discovery first, but I would not oppose clocks if the committee prefers a clean attribution.

responses.point: Johansson ranked circuit QED first, arguing it supplied the dispersive readout and bus architecture used by nearly every superconducting processor, and that it follows naturally from the 2025 prize.
responses.response: That is a strong technical case and the three-name theory-plus-experiment split is tidy. But I read the natural follow-on as exactly the risk: after 2025 the committee would be honouring the same community within a year, and Girvin and the Yale group are left unresolved. I would include it as an alternative rather than the lead.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can accept a three-person compromise from two collaborations of thousands, and whether Gianotti or Della Negra should take the third slot.
Whether the 2025 superconducting-circuits prize makes circuit QED too close, or on the contrary makes it timely.
Whether optical lattice clocks should wait for the redefinition of the second to show a concrete discovery payoff.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile; my documented connections (Gross, Rubinstein, Van Riet, Uppsala theory group) do not touch any shortlisted candidate.
